newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi charges 80 with murder of former leader.
newsitem.headline: Burundi charges 80 with murder of former leader.

text.p: Former army chief-of-staff Jean Bikomagu appeared in a Burundi court with 79 other people on Friday charged with the murder of Burundi's first freely-elected Hutu president Melchior Ndadaye.
Ndadaye's assassination by Tutsi troops in October 1993, three months after his election, sparked a bitter civil war in which more than 150,000 people have died.
The accused, who included former defence minister Charles Nteje, declared their innocence. The proceedings were adjourned until July 4.

Meantime police broke up a demonstration by hundreds of Tutsi students protesting against a peace initiative by military leader Pierre Buyoya, witnesses said. Several arrests were made. There were no immediate reports of casualties.

Buyoya was denounced as a traitor over peace negotiations with the main Hutu rebel group, the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD). Mediators said on Friday the two sides had agreed to try to restore peace through direct talks aimed at securing a lasting ceasefire.
